results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to produce time stamps for audit records; and b. Record, for audit records, those time stamps meeting [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] that satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint (CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint events) carry timestamps in ISO 8601 format with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix — e.g., '2025-12-01T11:00:00Z' and '2026-03-15T14:22:00Z'. This satisfies AU-8.r3(b)'s requirement to use Coordinated Universal Time. Timestamps are recorded to second-level granularity, which is substantive for audit purposes. CloudTrail is an AWS-managed service that relies on AWS's internal synchronized clocks (Amazon Time Sync Service / NTP), satisfying AU-8.r3(a)'s requirement to use internal system clocks. The timestamp format is consistent across all retrieved audit records, indicating a reliable and uniform implementation. Change-control anomalies noted in the evidence are relevant to other controls and do not affect this AU-8 assessment.
gaps: Organization-defined granularity requirement (the specific granularity threshold set by the organization) was not available — second-level granularity is assumed sufficient but formal policy confirmation would strengthen this finding.

No evidence of explicit NTP/time-sync configuration for any custom logging agents or containers running on the endpoint infrastructure — AWS CloudTrail itself is compliant, but workload-level clock synchronization was not directly verified.
